extents.other_hull_finding: the other hull (169748, the battle-mode mesh) has larger sorted spans than chassis box 0 at full length: [294.5, 492.92, 695.41] cm against [207.5, 374.54, 690.3] cm (worst deviation 0.419), and the box's intervals leave it by at most 0.0 cm - so the box sits inside that hull. The pursuit hull (169749) is the closer match. Recorded, not explained.
extents.reason: against the tight hull (169749) the full-length spans are within 30% on every axis (worst 0.150) while the half-length reading is 3.8x worse (0.575), and at full length every decoded box sits inside that hull's AABB to within 28.1 cm (4.2% of the hull's largest span) against 359.7 cm for the half-length reading
extents.rule: derived: compare sorted spans (frame-agnostic) of the chassis box with the union of the drivable collision hull's decoded element boxes. Full lengths hug the hull (ratio ~1); half lengths would be twice it.

wreck_conclusion.reason: read as full lengths the union of the 128 wreck boxes is [453.2, 197.09, 156.04] cm and read as half lengths [717.94, 394.18, 247.9] cm, against the intact car's hull [670.9457, 318.3124, 224.0855] cm: the half reading is the one that matches the intact car, the opposite of the chassis-box test. The wreck asset's boxes are per-bone envelopes of an exploded rig - the largest is 317.9422 cm on one axis while the translations span only [312.3, 79.3, 80.6] cm - so the assumption this comparison rests on (that those boxes tile the intact car) is not proven either way. Recorded; not used in the verdict.

wreck_union.label: derived: corners of every wreck box (identity rotation) at translation +/- e/2 (full lengths) and +/- e (half lengths)

orthonormality.label: derived: rows = floats[4i+1..4i+3] (reading A) give an orthonormal 3x3 with det +1 on every box; rows = floats[4i..4i+2] (reading B) do not. The four quad-leading floats are 0,0,0,1 in every box, which is the invariant that fixes which three floats of each quad are the row.
